extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR facilities, facility engineers and consultants (P.E.), environmental compliance staff, and contractors performing facility evaluations and monitoring
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing Facility Evaluation Reports (FER Part 1 and Part 2) and achieving regulatory compliance for CCR Management Units (CCRMU) under 40 CFR part 257, subpart D, including required documentation, certifications, monitoring, and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The name and address of the person(s) owning and operating the facility; the unit name associated with any regulated CCR unit and CCRMU containing one ton or more of CCR at the facility; and the identification number of each CCR unit and CCRMU if any have been assigned by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to uniquely identify facility ownership and each CCR unit/CCRMU (including state-assigned ID numbers) in the Part 2 FER.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 2) — location identification
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) The location of any CCRMU containing one ton or greater identified on the most recent U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) 7.5-minute or 15-minute topographic quadrangle map, or a topographic map of equivalent scale if a USGS map is not available. The location of each regulated CCR unit at the facility must also be identified in the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide map-based location for each CCRMU and regulated CCR unit using USGS (or equivalent) topo maps to allow spatial verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 3) — purpose statement
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) A statement of the purpose(s) for which each CCRMU at the facility is or was being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe historical and current uses of each CCRMU (e.g., storage, disposal, staging).

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 4) — foundation/abutment description
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) A description of the physical and engineering properties of the foundation and abutment materials on which each CCRMU was constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document geotechnical/engineering characteristics of the unit foundation and abutments relevant to stability and contaminant pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 5) — spills/releases and remediation evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) Any further evidence of known spills or releases of CCR, including any associated remediation activities, of CCR from each CCRMU and whether the spills or releases were reported to State or Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation of spills/releases, remediation history, and reporting records to authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 6) — structural instability evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) Any further evidence of structural instability of each CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report observed or documented indicators of structural issues (e.g., slumping, erosion, cracking).

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 7) — groundwater contamination evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) Any further evidence of groundwater contamination associated or potentially associated with each CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize groundwater data, previous monitoring results, or other indications of contamination linked to the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 8) — size and volume estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: (8) The size of each CCRMU, including the general lateral and vertical dimensions and an estimate of the volume of CCR contained within the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dimensional measurements and volume estimates (lateral/vertical extent and CCR volume) for each unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 9) — types of CCR identification
rubrics_metrics.description: (9) Identification of the types of CCR in each CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List CCR types (e.g., fly ash, bottom ash) present in each unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 10) — closure activities narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: (10) A narrative description of any closure activities that have occurred, including any applicable engineering drawings or reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe past closure work and attach engineering drawings, closure reports, or other relevant documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 11) — field oversight narrative & data reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: (11) A narrative that documents the nature and extent of field oversight activities and data reviewed as part of the facility evaluation process, and that lists all data and information that was reviewed indicating the presence or absence of CCRMU at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail what field oversight occurred (who, when, scope), list every data source reviewed, and state which pieces of information supported presence/absence conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 required contents (item 12) — supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: (12) Any additional supporting information used to identify and assess CCRMU at the facility, including but not limited to any construction diagrams, engineering drawings, permit documents, wastestream flow diagrams, aerial photographs, satellite images, historical facility maps, any field or analytical data, groundwater monitoring data or reports, inspection reports, documentation of interviews with current or former facility workers, and other documents or sources of information used to identify and assess CCRMU at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or reference all supporting documents (maps, photos, drawings, permits, interviews, lab data, monitoring reports, etc.) used in the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 1 — data gap remedy plan, operating record placement, and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 1 FER must be prepared and placed in the operating record and posted on the facility's website pursuant to §257.105(f) no later than 15 months after the effective date of the final rule; Part 1 should include the data gap remedy plan (detailed work plan including milestones and time frames).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 1 documents the results of records review and identification of data gaps and must present a detailed plan to remedy those gaps (contractor work plan, milestones, timeframes). It must be entered in the operating record and publicly posted within the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER Part 2 — narrative on how Part 1 data gaps were addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 2 of the FER must include a narrative that documents the nature and extent of field oversight activities and data reviewed as part of the facility evaluation process, and that lists all data and information reviewed that indicated the absence or presence of any CCRMU containing one ton or more of CCR at the facility. The narrative must also discuss how each data gap identified in Part 1 was addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 2 must describe fieldwork performed, data collected, how it fills Part 1 gaps, and any subsequent updates to Part 1/Part 2 as work changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No further testing required if no evidence after document review and visual inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after conducting a thorough document review and a visual inspection, the facility has found no evidence of any CCRMU, no further testing or sampling would be required to conclude that there is no CCRMU present at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is not requiring widespread site sampling to prove absence; however, all recorded observations and data from the evaluation must be assembled into the FER.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.E. certification requirement for FER (and role definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FER is required to include a certification from a P.E. stating that the FER meets the requirements at §257.75(c). The P.E.'s role is to act as an engineer in information collection, data gap identification, physical site inspection, and remedy of data gaps and certify accordingly; the P.E. is not making final determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.E. must be a licensed professional engineer qualified by training and experience and subject to a code of ethics and licensure penalties; EPA rejected modifying certification language and expects P.E. certifications as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and posting of FERs in operating record and CCR website (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the information gathering part of the facility evaluation process, owners or operators must compile and place in the operating record information pertaining to every CCRMU containing one ton or more of CCR no later than the applicable deadline. Both Part 1 and Part 2 of the FER must be posted to the facility's CCR publicly accessible internet site within 30 days of that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERs must be available in the operating record and posted publicly on the facility website promptly (posting within 30 days of the compliance date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of existing Part 257 requirements to CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing that CCRMU must comply with fugitive dust, groundwater monitoring, corrective action, closure, post-closure care, recordkeeping, notification, and internet posting requirements. Other existing requirements in part 257, subpart D (e.g., structural stability, location restrictions, liner design) are not generally necessary for CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the listed existing requirements to CCRMU at active facilities and certain inactive facilities; structural stability, liner, and location restrictions are generally inappropriate because CCRMU are not operational or will be required to close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fugitive dust requirements apply and plan amendment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators are required to minimize CCR fugitive dust originating from the facility under §257.80. EPA is finalizing an amendment to §257.80(b)(6) to require owners or operators to amend the fugitive dust plan no later than 30 days following a triggering event, such as the closure of a CCR unit or change in facility or CCR unit operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fugitive dust control applies facility-wide (units, roads, handling). Facilities must update their fugitive dust control plan within 30 days after triggering events; EPA declined broader notification/air monitoring changes absent factual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements (§§257.90-257.98) apply to CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing that CCRMU must comply with the existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action criteria in §§257.90 through 257.98, with one revision to require sampling and analysis of constituents listed in Appendix IV at the same time as those listed in Appendix III and adopting combined detection and assessment monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must install monitoring wells, follow sampling procedures, analyze for Appendix III and Appendix IV constituents simultaneously, evaluate data for SSIs and SSLs, and implement corrective action under §§257.96-257.98 when GWPS exceedances occur. EPA rejected proposals for alternative/risk-based groundwater standards absent specific justification and supports tailored remedies through existing corrective action provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single (consolidated) deadline for groundwater monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a single deadline for the groundwater monitoring requirements (instead of the proposed two separate deadlines) to allow flexibility for activities like well installation, sampling, and receipt of lab results which are susceptible to factors outside a facility's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single consolidated deadline affords facilities regional flexibility (seasonality, permitting, contractor availability) while maintaining protection; EPA found two split deadlines infeasible and lacking a clear compliance verification mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final compliance time frames for CCRMU (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final schedule of required deliverables measured in months after the effective date of the final rule (rule effective six months after publication): Internet Posting (§257.107) — 15 months; FER Part 1 — 15 months; FER Part 2 — 27 months; Install groundwater monitoring system (§257.91) — 42 months; Develop groundwater sampling & analysis program — 42 months; Initiate detection/assessment monitoring — 42 months; Complete initial annual GWMCA report — January 31, 2029; Prepare written closure plan (§257.102) — 48 months; Prepare written post-closure care plan (§257.104) — 48 months; Initiate closure (§§257.101/257.102) — 54 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are measured from the effective date; final rule effective six months after publication, so facilities have an extra six months beyond the listed deadlines. EPA considered contractor shortages, seasonality, and other constraints in setting extended deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of resource and timing constraints in schedule setting
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA extended and restructured FER timelines (two-part FER) and other deadlines after considering commenters' concerns about contractor shortages/backlogs, seasonality, difficulty accessing historical information, overlapping regulatory requirements, and quality assurance/time needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory deadlines reflect practical implementation constraints; facilities should plan for contractor mobilization times, permitting, seasonality, and QA/QC when scheduling work and updating public FERs as field work evolves.
